New 4th peer: **mpdecimal / libmpdec 4.0.1** (Stefan Krah), static -O3 archive at ~/libmpdec, pinned to `mpd_ieee_context(&c,128)`; joins libbid + decQuad (decNumber). bench_libbid_vs_d128 --benchmark_repetitions=10 --benchmark_report_aggregates_only --benchmark_min_time=0.2s; ns/op = median_ns / 4096. harness note:  **`CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` is NOT sufficient on this setup** — the Release per-config CXX flags did not reach the CXX targets, so `bench_main.cpp` (the timed 4096-op loop) compiled at **-O0** and the FetchContent'd google-benchmark library built **without NDEBUG** ("***WARNING*** Library was built as DEBUG"). That fixed harness overhead is added to every arm, **compressing ratios ~30%** (add-SQ read 2.15× instead of 3.17×, mul-CP 4.13× instead of 7.72×). Putting `-O3 -DNDEBUG` explicitly in both flag vars removes the warning and restores the `xc`-consistent ratios. The C `core` lib was unaffected (it carries its own Release flags). New mpdecimal arm (§4.1/4.2/4.3, rows tagged xc2): d128 leads it every band **1.89×–14.22×**, narrowest at div CD (shared compact-divide cost), widest at div PT (`divPow10Divisor` early-out); libmpdec carries the Cowlishaw divide signature (CD < WD < XD). d128 **wins mul XP vs libmpdec (3.42×)** — libmpdec's wide multiply is costlier than software DPD, mirroring the arm64 `Rmpd` finding.
